title: Cross-SDK resilient defaults and idempotency semantics with multi-lang examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement cross-SDK defaults for retry/backoff, idempotency key handling, and a retryable-error taxonomy that is consistent across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Deliverables: 1) Spec for default retry/backoff (parameters + rationale), 2) Concrete idempotency semantics and header/param conventions for both unary and streaming APIs, 3) Canonical retryable error classification and mapping to HTTP/gRPC/transport errors, 4) Example snippets and a reference test suite across all three SDKs, 5) Backwards-compatible rollout plan and migration guidance for existing customers.

Scope: Network-level and server transient errors (5xx, 429), client-side timeouts, partial streaming disconnects. Include guidance for long-running streaming responses and when to allow automatic retries vs when to surface to callers. Non-goal: Changing server-side API surface or enforcement of idempotency keys at the API gateway (this ticket focuses on SDK behavior and docs).
acceptance_criteria: A unified spec document checked into docs/confluence with tested defaults and examples
SDK implementations in python/typescript/go include the defaults behind feature flags and pass the cross-SDK test suite
Examples demonstrate idempotent create semantics using Idempotency-Key header and non-idempotent streaming examples with explicit client guidance
Migration guide + changelog entry and deprecation timeline if defaults change
Manual QA checklist executed and sign-off from SDK lead and PM
decisions: Default retry strategy: jittered exponential backoff with base=200ms, factor=2.0, max_backoff=8s, max_retries=3 for idempotent/unary calls
Non-idempotent or streaming start requests will default to no automatic retries; SDKs will expose an opt-in 'at_least_once' helper for advanced users
Idempotency key convention: use 'Idempotency-Key' header for HTTP transports and metadata 'idempotency-key' for gRPC. SDKs will canonicalize user-provided header keys and send consistently.
Retryable error taxonomy: transient_network, server_overload (429), server_error_5xx, connection_reset, timeout, kv-cache-miss (internal transient) mapped to unified labels
Streaming rules: resumable streams are opt-in and require server support; by default, streaming responses are treated as non-idempotent and will not be retried automatically

examples: Python (unary, idempotent): client.generate(prompt="...", headers={'Idempotency-Key': id_key}) - SDK auto-applies retry policy for 5xx/429 up to max_retries
TypeScript (unary, idempotent): await client.generate({ prompt }, { idempotencyKey: idKey }) - maps to 'Idempotency-Key' header; retry policy applied
Go (streaming start, non-idempotent): stream, err := client.StreamCreate(ctx, req) - no auto-retry on disconnect; recommend user re-open stream with application-level resume token if supported
Streaming resume pattern (opt-in): server returns resume_token on stream; client may call ResumeStream(resume_token) with explicit at_least_once helper
migration_notes: Defaults behind feature flags so customers can opt-in before GA
Deprecation window: 90 days after GA for changing defaults; provide CLI and SDK toggles to restore legacy behavior
Changelog entries will include explicit guidance on how to opt out for latency-sensitive workloads
